column1: # Built by build_srange_reference.py in this directory; read that file's
# header for the method, the convergence-escalation scheme, and why it is
# independent of both R's stats::ptukey and scipy.stats.studentized_range.
# Points that did not converge to the 1e-12 relative target within the
# escalation budget are named in '#'-prefixed "OPEN POINT" lines at the end
# of this file (search for that string) and are NOT data rows here.
# The prior file had 48/107 rows at mpmath_converged=False (most ~6.6e-11
# agreement, short of the file's own 1e-12 rule) plus 4 quantile cells
# (k in {3,5}, df in {3,10}, p_target=1e-5) whose stored q solved to
# mpmath_p ~1.0024e-5 against a 1e-5 target -- not the file's own equation.
# Root cause found and fixed (see gl_nodes' docstring in the builder): the
# Gauss-Legendre nodes/weights driving EVERY quadrature in this file were
# computed at float64 precision (scipy.special.roots_legendre) and merely
# cast into mpmath, capping achievable accuracy at roughly that ~1e-14
# floor regardless of degree or dps -- confirmed by a non-monotone drift
# in relative agreement as degree rose (3.8e-9 -> 8.6e-10 -> 2.3e-9 on the
# worst measured cell), the signature of a precision floor, not a
# resolution problem. Nodes/weights are now Newton-polished to the AMBIENT
# working precision from the same float64 starting guesses; the same
# fixed breakpoint/tier structure then converges cleanly (verified: 30
# stable digits across degree 40/56/72 on that same cell, no other change).
# Two extra escalation tiers (5, 6; see TIERS in the builder) were added as
# margin on top of the fix, and cleared every row except three: k=10,
# tier 6 -- the single deepest p_target combined with the largest k in
# the grid). Two more tiers (7, 8) were then added and DID clear those
# three (agree 3.0e-23, 6.4e-24, 5.0e-24 at tier 7) -- no row in this
# grid ended up a genuine open point. The quantile inverter's one-shot
# secant correction was replaced by a real iterative secant loop run to
# convergence before the final accepted evaluation (see invert_q_for_p) --
# this is what re-solves the four quantile cells named above to their
# targets (measured: mpmath_p now matches p_target to ~1e-11 to 1e-19
# relative, down from up to 0.24% off).
# k=2 ROWS (RULING_WAVE_THREE Q3): at k=2 the studentized range is EXACTLY
# sqrt(2) times a Student-t(df) variate (Q = sqrt(2)*|T|, since the range
# of two iid N(0,1) is sqrt(2)*|Z| and Z/S ~ t(df)). Where an exact
# identity exists the owned kernel uses it, so k=2 rows in this file are
# now computed from that identity (mpmath's own regularized incomplete
# beta function -- see p_upper_k2_exact in the builder), NOT from the
# general double-integral quadrature and NOT from R's approximate qtukey.
# This is a genuine, not merely more-precise, change of reference value at
# k=2 -- calibration (the ruling's own numbers): qtukey(0.95,2,17) =
# 2.9837298042779 (exact), 3.2e-8 apart. See the "K=2 ROWS CHANGED" note
# directly below for exactly which rows moved and by how much under this
# switch -- it changes what the port is judged against at k=2, so it is
# recorded here, not just in the commit.
# For k=2 rows, mpmath_quad_tier reads "exact+N" (N = extra precision
# steps beyond the base dps) rather than a TIERS index, since there is no
# K=2 ROWS CHANGED -- measured, this regeneration (all 20 k=2 forward rows;
# there are no k=2 rows in the quantile grid). Two comparisons matter:
#  (a) vs this file's OWN prior (unconverged, general-double-integral)
#      value, for the 12 rows that existed before: the numerical MOVE is
#      tiny (1.4e-9 relative at the worst, down to 7e-14 at ordinary p) --
#      expected, since the old value was already a close approximation to
#      the same exact quantity, just short of the 1e-12 bar. This is NOT
#      the number that matters for acceptance.
#  (b) vs R's stats::ptukey at the SAME (k=2,df,q) -- THE number that
#      changes what the port is judged against, per Q3. At ordinary p
#      (0.1, 1e-4) R's k=2 approximation is close, matching the ruling's
#      own 3.2e-8-at-df=17 calibration in order of magnitude:
#        df=3,  p=0.1:    rel diff 1.5e-12   df=10, p=0.1:    rel diff 3.2e-10
#        df=45, p=0.1:    rel diff 5.7e-12   df=200,p=0.1:    rel diff 5.4e-13
#        df=45, p=1e-4:   rel diff 3.7e-09   df=200,p=1e-4:   rel diff 6.3e-10
#      In the far tail R's OWN cancellation problem (documented elsewhere
#      in this kit, unrelated to the k=2 approximation itself) dominates
#      and the gap grows to orders of magnitude, e.g.:
#      below and compare column 7 (mpmath_p, now exact) against column 16
#      note -- it is still R-vs-scipy agreement, both approximate at k=2;
#      whether the port's acceptance script should stop trusting that flag
#      at k=2 (since R is no longer the intended oracle there per Q3) is a
#      question for whoever next touches validate/v154, not this file.
# FORWARD ROWS ARE NOMINAL, EXCEPT TWO CELLS NOW ROOT-SOLVED (RULING
# diagnosis). Read this before trusting p_target on any "forward" row.
# EVERY OTHER forward row in this file is SEEDED, not solved: main()
# picks q = scipy.stats.studentized_range.isf(p_target, k, df) and simply
# records whatever true probability that q happens to give as mpmath_p.
# p_target is therefore a NOMINAL label, accurate only to the extent
# scipy's inverse is accurate at that (k, df, p) -- true almost everywhere
# in this grid, since scipy's isf is close except at the corner this file
# exists to probe (small df, deep p). It is NOT true at k=10, df=3 deep in
# the tail: scipy's isf is off there by up to 100%, so the seeded q's
# mpmath_p can land an order of magnitude from its own p_target with
# nothing in the row flagging it. Do not assume p_target == mpmath_p for
# any "forward" row without checking; compare the two columns yourself.
# THE TWO k=10, df=3 CELLS AT p_target IN {1e-10, 1e-15} are the
# exception: both are now genuinely ROOT-SOLVED for q, per the ruling.
# verification step this regeneration added because invert_q_for_p's
# internal secant runs on a cheap, non-maximal tier (TIERS[3]) whose own
# "converged" self-check is not trustworthy this deep -- proved directly:
# at p_target=1e-15 the cheap-tier candidate root reported converged and
# was still 34% off in p when checked with a FULL escalated evaluation):
#   1. qGuess = scipy isf(p_target, k, df) (starting point only).
#      not just the cheap one) at qGuess -- point A.
#   3. Candidate root qStar from invert_q_for_p, which itself ends in one
#      full escalated evaluation at qStar -- point B.
#   4. If point B's mpmath_p disagrees with p_target by more than 1e-6
#      relative, take ONE secant step in log(q)/log(p) space using points
#      A and B (both fully escalated, never the cheap tier), then a final
#      full escalated evaluation at the corrected q.
# Measured this regeneration (see the two "forward B 10 3" rows below):
#   p_target=1e-10: candidate root (step 3) already agreed to 2.6e-7
#     relative -- no correction step needed. q = 7865.71047518377,
#     above, reproduced directly. The log(q)/log(p) secant correction
#     agree_prev_tier = 2.44e-23. This q is roughly 46x the seeded q
#     scipy's isf had picked for this row before -- these are genuinely
#     different cells now, not a refinement of the old ones.
# Both cells' q changed substantially from the prior (seeded) values, so
# after this regeneration; re-run it rather than assuming the prior
# NOT DONE HERE, AND DELIBERATELY: no other forward row in this file was
# re-solved by this pass. Whether the rest of the forward half should be
# root-solved too is the open question in MEMO_GRID_ROWS_NEVER_SOLVED --
# out of scope for the two named cells this pass was ordered to fix.
#   chosen, q solved by bisection against this file's own mpmath integral;
#   mpmath_p is the converged P(Q>q) at the solved q, which should equal
#   p_target to mpmath_agree_prev_tier's precision -- both are reported so
#   a reader can check the inversion's own consistency directly).
# tier: which coverage tier this cell came from (A=broad, B=far-tail-focus,
# k, df: distribution parameters. p_target: the p this cell targets (forward:
#   what q was chosen to hit; quantile: what q was solved for). q: the
#   studentized-range statistic evaluated at (forward) or solved for
# mpmath_p: this file's own converged reference value of P(Q>q).
# mpmath_dps: working decimal precision used for the accepted evaluation.
# mpmath_quad_tier: which escalation tier (1-8, TIERS in the builder) the
#   accepted value came from; for k=2 rows (exact identity, no quadrature)
#   this instead reads "exact+N", N = extra precision steps used past the
# mpmath_agree_prev_tier: relative agreement between the accepted tier and
#   the one before it -- THE CONVERGENCE EVIDENCE. <=1e-12 when
#   mpmath_converged is True; may be looser (never above 1e-6 -- points
#   that bad are OPEN POINTs, excluded) when tier escalation hit its cap
#   before reaching 1e-12; reported honestly either way.
#   quantile rows), for reference -- NOT the acceptance oracle here.
# mc_p, mc_se, mc_n: Monte Carlo estimate of P(Q>q) by direct simulation
#   (independent normals for the range, an independent chi(df) draw for the
#   scale, empirical exceedance count) with its standard error and draw
#   count. NaN/0 when p is below ~1e-6 (not enough draws are affordable for
#   a meaningful SE there -- reported as missing, not as a padded number).
# r_ptukey_p: R's stats::ptukey(q,k,df,lower.tail=FALSE) at this exact q,
# r_in_verified_domain: whether THIS EXACT (k,df,q) point passes the
#   standard rule against scipy, live -- the operational domain test from
#   R_verified_domain.tsv's header (not a table lookup; see that file for
#   why). True means R may be used as oracle here per the governing ruling;
#   False means acceptance for this cell is against mpmath_p only.
# wall_sec: wall-clock time this file's own mpmath computation took for
#   the accepted tier (does not include scipy/MC/R side computations).
